nodes.label: Frontend-Only-Rendering Architecture Principle
nodes.rationale: Frontend handles only rendering and UI interaction; all functional operations must be delegated to the Rust backend via IPC. This separates concerns cleanly and enables performance optimizations like zero-copy stats on Rust-side ropes.

nodes.label: Code Organization Principle (AI-Friendly)
nodes.rationale: Single-file bloat is prohibited. AI reads small files more efficiently within context windows. Rust files >500 lines and frontend files >400 lines must be split. This is the highest priority for codebase maintainability.

nodes.label: Document Registry (Rust Rope)
nodes.rationale: Rust holds a rope copy of each document (HashMap<tab_id, Document>). Stats and search compute directly on rope without full-text IPC transfer, achieving zero-copy performance.

nodes.label: Instant Render Plugin
nodes.rationale: Typora-style rendering: shows Markdown syntax near cursor, hides it elsewhere. Uses incremental decoration updates on affected top-level blocks only, avoiding full-document traversal.

nodes.label: Rust Desktop Shell (wry + tao)
nodes.rationale: Uses wry (WebView) + tao (window management) instead of Electron/Tauri for a lightweight native desktop shell.

nodes.label: Outline Extraction (Zero IPC)
nodes.rationale: Outline is extracted directly from ProseMirror doc.descendants() on the frontend. This is the only exception to the 'all ops via IPC' rule because it is pure local rendering logic with no backend dependency.
